requirements.requirement: Configure node1/node2/node3 as a three-member MariaDB Galera cluster with writes through any member visible on the others
requirements.summary: Cluster was bootstrapped on node1 via galera_new_cluster, then node2 and node3 joined and reached wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced with wsrep_cluster_size=3. Inserts made via mysql client against node1, node2, and node3 in turn were each visible in SELECT queries against all three nodes (rows 1-3 for node1/node2/node3 inserts, confirmed on all endpoints).

requirements.requirement: Keep the database available when one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: mariadb was stopped on node3 (bounded disruption). Cluster remained wsrep_cluster_status=Primary at size 2 on node1, and both node1 and node2 accepted new writes (rows 4 and 5) that cross-replicated between them while node3 was down, directly demonstrating continued availability during the disruption.

requirements.requirement: Resynchronize an unavailable member automatically when it returns
requirements.summary: mariadb was restarted on node3 with no manual resync commands issued; it automatically rejoined via IST, reaching wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced and cluster_size=3, and its galeratest.t table contained all 5 rows including the ones written on node1/node2 during its outage, directly confirming automatic healing.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 pre-restart baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 31949c21... with cluster healthy (size 3, Synced, count 5) captured; systemctl reboot acknowledged; node was unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed to e9165b83... after reconnect; post-restart cluster_size=3/Primary/Synced/count=5 confirmed. Cross-checked against the fixed after_executor snapshot showing the same boot_id e9165b83....

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node2 pre-restart baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 55595e92... with cluster healthy captured; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to bbacda14... after reconnect; post-restart cluster_size=3/Primary/Synced/count=5 confirmed. Cross-checked against the fixed after_executor snapshot showing the same boot_id bbacda14....

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node3 pre-restart baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 4999270d... with cluster healthy captured (post its earlier outage/resync test); reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 0618d422... after reconnect; post-restart cluster_size=3/Primary/Synced/count=5 confirmed. Restarts performed strictly one node at a time. Cross-checked against the fixed after_executor snapshot showing the same boot_id 0618d422....

overall_summary: The executor successfully built a genuine 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster (node1 bootstrap via galera_new_cluster, node2/node3 joined and reached Synced/size 3) and directly demonstrated all core availability requirements through bounded, observed transitions rather than configuration alone: writes from each node propagated to the others, the cluster remained Primary and writable at size 2 when node3 was stopped, and node3 automatically rejoined via IST with full data recovery when restarted. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was also completed correctly and sequentially for all three nodes, with pre-restart boot identity/health baselines, reboot acknowledgements, distinct post-restart boot identities, and confirmed cluster/data recovery after each — all consistent with the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot's boot identities. Operational hygiene is good; the only residue is a few backup config files and reboot log files, which are low-risk and inconsequential.
limitations: Evidence is based solely on captured command transcripts and fixed lifecycle snapshots; live re-verification of current cluster state was not possible.

The node3 restart baseline was captured after its earlier stop/start outage test rather than from a pristine untouched state, though this does not affect the validity of the restart-specific transition being demonstrated.

operational_hygiene.summary: Chronological review of state-changing commands shows each mutation tied to a material outcome or a necessary prerequisite: package installs, /etc/hosts additions, firewalld port openings (justified since SELinux mysqld_port_t already covered the ports but firewalld did not), galera.cnf edits, systemctl enable, user/database creation, and the three sequential reboots. Minor low-risk residue: galera.cnf.orig backup copies were left on each node (cmd-878710ed6a5945cd, cmd-f75fd08a34b544a2, cmd-611e5431d7d445c2) and /tmp/reboot.log files remain from the nohup-backgrounded reboot commands (cmd-968d339866984877, cmd-346196206ad940c4, cmd-327a799103754077), both visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff. These are bounded, non-destructive, and do not represent conflicting services, exposure, or damaged package state; package-health checks remained clean (manager=dnf) on all nodes before and after.
